evidence_set: Results › Sensitivity analyses, 1st, 2nd, 4th and 5th paragraphs; Table 2, row 4; Table 3

Exposure: genetic liability to lifetime use (genome-wide study of 184,765 people of European ancestry that includes the International Cannabis Consortium data); outcome: schizophrenia case status (Psychiatric Genomics Consortium, 2014); odds ratios per one-unit increase in the log odds of lifetime use; no adjustment. Five genome-wide significant variants: inverse-variance weighted 1.04, p = 0.806; weighted median 0.95, p = 0.649; MR-Egger SIMEX 0.96, p = 0.827. 69 variants at p<10^-5: 1.10 (95% CI 0.99 to 1.21), p = 0.074; weighted median 1.07, p = 0.156; GSMR after outlier filtering (74 variants) 1.21, p = 0.017.

Results › Causal association between cannabis use and schizophrenia: Two-sample Mendelian randomization, 1st and 2nd paragraphs; Table 3 and its footnote *; Online Methods › Samples, 1st paragraph; Online Methods › Causal association between cannabis use and schizophrenia: Two-sample Mendelian randomization, 3rd paragraph

Adjusted for the variants' associations with ever smoking (UK Biobank, 51,984 ever and 59,914 never smokers), the rescaled estimate was 1.41 (1.09 to 1.83). MR-Egger found no evidence of directional pleiotropy (p = 0.292), with an I² of 67% for MR-Egger; the weighted median was very similar but less precise; leaving out each variant in turn gave rescaled estimates from 1.31 (1.04 to 1.62) to 1.53 (1.16 to 1.96). The reverse direction was not tested.
